blurb:
Marietta Melt Yard on Whitlock is a solid group lunch spot. We've ended up there with family a couple of times now and it works well when you've got different ages and appetites at the same table. The service has been good both times, and the staff is clearly used to handling a crowd.

The food leans on the heavier, greasier side, so if you're going in expecting something light, just know what you're getting into. That said, people keep going back, and for that kind of casual, comfort-food situation it does the job. Worth trying if you haven't been.

Friday and Saturday they stay open until 10pm, which makes it a decent option if you're eating late on a weekend.

blurb:
If you want a high-energy place to watch a game or hang out on a weekend night with a cold beer in your hand, The Wing Cafe and Tap House on Roswell Road is the move. They've got an outdoor tiki bar, live music, and the kind of crowd that's clearly there to have a good time. It's loud and fun. Not a quiet dinner spot, but that's not what it's trying to be.

The wings are the main event, obviously. Over 1,900 reviews and a 4.4 star rating says people aren't leaving disappointed. The craft beer selection gives you options beyond the usual suspects, which I appreciate.

They're open until 11pm every night of the week, so it also works as a late-night stop after whatever else you had going on.

blurb:
JJ's Pizzeria is the kind of neighborhood pizza spot that's been quietly doing it right for a long time. It's in a strip mall on Roswell Road, and inside it's got that homey, hole-in-the-wall feel that you just can't fake. The staff is genuinely friendly and the place has a relaxed vibe that makes it easy to stay longer than you planned.

The garlic knots are a must. Messy, yes, but absolutely worth it. My wife and I usually get a large pizza and an order of knots and that's the whole plan for the evening. The buffalo chicken pizza has a following for good reason, and people who've added jalapeños to it swear by the combination. Generous toppings across the board, which matters.

Just know they're closed Tuesdays, so plan around that if Tuesday is your pizza night.

blurb:
This one is a genuine hidden gem on Allgood Road, and I say that because most people drive right past it without knowing there's a taqueria inside. It's a supermarket with a kitchen in the back, and the food coming out of that kitchen is seriously good.

The al pastor is what you want. People who review this place consistently call it out as the best meat they offer, and from what I've heard it's well seasoned and cooked perfectly without being overdone. The pupusas are another must, specifically the beans and cheese. Homemade beans, not from a can, which you can taste immediately. The chicken plate with rice and beans is also worth ordering if you want something more filling.

Thursday hours are shorter than the rest of the week, so plan accordingly if that's your day.

blurb:
This place has become a regular stop for me on weekday mornings when I want something other than a drive-through coffee and a sad granola bar. Brazilian Bakery Cafe on Powers Ferry is the kind of spot where you walk in and immediately feel like you stumbled onto something good. Cheery, colorful, and busy in the best way.

The Brazilian light bites are what keep people coming back. Traditional cakes, cookies, and savory baked goods that you're not going to find at your average coffee shop. My wife loves the sweet stuff here. The cookies especially. And the prices are inexpensive enough that grabbing a few things to bring home doesn't feel like a decision.

They're open seven days a week from early morning until 10pm, so it works whether you're grabbing a quick breakfast before work or stopping in after dinner because you want something sweet. Really solid neighborhood find.
